card: Adds an optional build-time script execution tracing hook to the script interpreter, exposed via the libbitcoinkernel C API and C++ wrapper. External kernel consumers cannot currently inspect intermediate execution states, precluding the development of script debuggers, and interpreter tests can miss bugs shadowed by later failure conditions. The author provides a proof-of-concept debugger using rust-bitcoinkernel to demonstrate practical utility. The feature is disabled by default in CMake builds and has no dependencies.
changed_since_previous: No substantial functional or architectural changes; updated via rebase and minor cleanups.
evidence: The author demonstrates functionality with a prototype debugger implementation in rust-bitcoinkernel (cited in the PR description).
The PR description cites PR #33961 as an example where unit test bugs occurred because later error conditions shadowed unintended intermediate interpreter behavior.
problem: External applications utilizing libbitcoinkernel cannot inspect intermediate script execution states, preventing them from implementing script debuggers or fine-grained execution analyzers. Additionally, testing and fuzzing harness code cannot easily observe interpreter behavior when later error conditions shadow intermediate bugs.

risk.why: Mistakes in interpreter tracing macros or build guards could inadvertently alter script evaluation execution paths or introduce bugs in sensitive validation code.

scope_notes: Touches the core script interpreter (`src/script/interpreter.cpp`) to place macro hooks, but execution overhead is compiled out by default via CMake configuration.
summary: Adds an optional compile-time script execution tracing framework exposed through the libbitcoinkernel C API and its C++ wrapper. When built with `-DENABLE_SCRIPT_TRACE=ON`, hooks in `EvalScript` invoke a registered callback with execution state snapshots (stack, altstack, opcode, execution condition, tapleaf hash, and errors) before and after execution as well as at each evaluation step. When the build flag is omitted, the interpreter hooks compile down to no-ops.
